gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns undefined L2 residual and reconstruction quantities for general H^{-1} data, whereas ISSUE-001 concerns the invalid L-infinity embedding needed for quasilinear C3 estimates. These are different mathematical objects and failed obligations.

The gold issue is the incompatibility and nonuniqueness of an auxiliary CR problem on the unrestricted space because constants lie in its kernel. ISSUE-002 instead diagnoses a sign/orientation mismatch in the adjoint residual reconstruction; it does not recognize the CR solvability or boundary-space defect.
Both identify that the claimed quasilinear C3 estimate on H_0^1 in dimensions two and three relies on an unavailable uniform L-infinity bound, so the advertised certification is unsupported.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The quasilinear C3 verification requires uniform L-infinity control on H_0^1 balls in dimensions two and three, but such control fails; consequently the stated C3 certificate is not established on the claimed space.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claimed L-infinity estimate on H_0^1 in dimensions two and three is unavailable, so the derivation of the quasilinear operator/C3 bound fails.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-001 explicitly identifies the nonexistent H_0^1-to-L-infinity bound, its use throughout the Lipschitz/C3 derivation, and the resulting vacuity of the claimed certification.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify that the printed adjoint residual reconstruction mixes incompatible source signs and flux orientations, so the displayed mismatch and residual do not bound the norm of G as claimed.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The computable adjoint-residual majorant uses a source/sign convention inconsistent with the chosen residual orientation, making the reconstructed residual and mismatch fail to certify the true adjoint residual norm.

component_coverage.gold_component: The source term and flux mismatch are inconsistent with the orientation of G, so the displayed majorant does not bound ||G(z_h)||.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-002 derives the residual after integration by parts, shows that the prescribed divergence gives the wrong residual for G, identifies that the theorem applies only to -G with the opposite source, and supplies the consistent repair.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-004 recognizes that the admissible set can have a closed upper endpoint and that the interval description needs endpoint qualifications. It does not recognize the distinct tangential singleton case or the required separate nondegeneracy treatment, so it covers only part of the bundled gold concern.
